task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: I'm sorry to hear that, John — let's get this sorted out. First, let me look up your account.

turns.thought:
I found the reason your line has no service, John:

- Your line 555-123-2002 (line L1002) was suspended today, and there is also an overdue bill of $65.00 (bill B1234321, due January 15).
- I've sent a payment request for that overdue bill to your account — please accept it so the charge can be paid.

turns.execution_output: User: Oh my, suspended? I had no idea there was an overdue bill. I'm sorry about that. Let me see if I can find this payment request you sent.

turns.thought:
Your payment of $65.00 has gone through and the bill is now marked Paid. I've also lifted the suspension on your line 555-123-2002 — it's now Active.

Since your phone was in Airplane Mode, you'll need to turn that off. I can't change that setting from my side, so please go to your phone's Settings and switch **Airplane Mode** to OFF (it's usually at the top of the Settings menu, or in the quick settings panel if you swipe down from the top of the screen).

Once that's off, please restart (reboot) your phone so it can reconnect to the network. After it powers back on, check whether the signal bars have returned.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me try turning off that airplane mode first. I'll do one thing at a time so I don't get mixed up.

turns.thought:
I checked on my side, and your line 555-123-2002 is showing as Active now — the suspension has been lifted and your data usage is fine (8.7 GB of your 15 GB allowance), so that's not the cause.

To answer your question first: restarting your phone will not delete your photos, or anything else. A restart just turns the phone off and back on again — your pictures, contacts, and apps all stay exactly where they are. It's a very common step and it's safe.

I wasn't able to adjust the phone's other settings remotely (my system couldn't reach those controls on your device). The "Data Disabled" indication on your phone is something that needs to be turned on from the phone itself:

1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (or **Connections** / **Mobile Network** depending on your phone)
3. Tap **Mobile Data** (or **Cellular Data**)
4. Switch it **ON**

Then, if you're comfortable, restart your phone so it can reconnect to the network. Let me know how it goes — if you still have no signal after that, I'll arrange for a human agent to look into it further with you.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, thank you for explaining that about the photos — that makes me feel better. Let me try turning on the mobile data thing.

turns.thought:
Yes, John — go ahead and restart it now. It's safe, and your photos, contacts, and everything else on the phone will be exactly as you left them. A restart just powers the phone off and back on; it doesn't erase anything.

To do it:

1. Press and hold the **Power** button (usually on the right side of the phone) for a few seconds.
2. When the menu appears, tap **Restart** (or **Power off**, then press and hold Power again to turn it back on).
3. Wait about a minute for it to fully start back up.

Once it's back on, check the top of the screen and let me know what it shows — whether you now see signal bars, whether data is enabled, and whether there's still an airplane symbol.

I want to be straight with you: I haven't been able to reach the settings controls on your device from my side, so if the signal doesn't come back after this restart, I'll transfer you to a human agent who can dig into it further with you.
